question.text: How many shrimp per year will be covered by SWP's Humane Slaughter Initiative agreements on July 1, 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the Shrimp Welfare Project's estimated "[Shrimpact](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)" (in billions of shrimp helped in expectation per year) when checked by Metaculus on or soon after July 1, 2027.
question.fine_print:
The question will resolve as the headline estimated Shrimpact, regardless of any estimated range. If SWP ceases to provide a headline estimate and instead provides only a range, however, the question will resolve as the midpoint of the range.

The total Shrimpact will be rounded, if necessary, to the nearest 100 million shrimp.

research:
## SWP Shrimpact forecast research (as of 2026-11-11)

The headline figure is now about 6.5 billion shrimp per year. That is below the question's lower bound of 6.95 billion. Over the last 14 months it has grown by roughly 0.18 billion a month.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-11 (fetched today): the [Shrimpact page](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact) gives a headline of **about 6.5 billion shrimp helped per year in expectation**, with a range of 4.5 to 9 billion. Cost-effectiveness is about 1,400 shrimp per $ per year. The page shows no date. An image filename mentions "oct 2026", which suggests an October 2026 update.
  - The page reports 37 corporate agreements across 9 countries, covering about 89,774 metric tonnes a year once all stunners are running.
  - 20 stunners are installed and commissioned, covering about 54,175 t, or roughly 3.6 billion shrimp. The rest are in production, shipping, customs or waiting for commissioning.
  - Breakdown by country: Vietnam ~2.54B, Honduras ~1.30B, India ~0.63B, Indonesia ~0.57B, Ecuador ~0.48B, Sri Lanka ~0.44B, Venezuela ~0.28B, Thailand ~0.18B, Nigeria ~0.07B.
  - The figure is a projection from signed commitments, so it counts agreements, not shrimp actually stunned. Retailer policies are not included.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The current value (6.5B) sits about 0.45B below the question's lower bound. Getting above it needs a few more agreements, or one large one.
- The number moves upward in steps when new agreements are signed. It could also be revised down through methodology changes, but I found no example of a downward revision.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- About Oct 2026: the Shrimpact page rose to 6.5B with 37 agreements, and Honduras, Ecuador, Venezuela and Nigeria now appear. I could find no press releases announcing these Latin American or African partners. [Shrimpact](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)
- 2026-09: the question background puts the figure at 6.3B.
- 2026-08: an ACE report, as cited on Wikipedia, gives about 6.1B once all equipment is running. I could not check the ACE source directly. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrimp_Welfare_Project)
- First half of 2026: 33 MOUs signed. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrimp_Welfare_Project)
  - SeafoodSource reported a "30th MoU", but I couldn't open the page (403), so I don't have its date. [SeafoodSource](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/aquaculture/uk-nonprofit-ensuring-viability-of-shrimp-welfare-commitments-through-electrical-stunner-agreements)
- 2026-01-14: Trang Corporation and Dary Foods joined, committing to stun 1,800 t a year. This was the 25th partnership. SWP's press-release page has listed nothing newer since. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/trangs-group-trang-corporation-dary-foods-join-humane-slaughter-partnership-with-shrimp-welfare-project), [GSA](https://www.globalseafood.org/advocate/leading-vietnamese-shrimp-producer-commits-to-humane-slaughter/)
- 2025-12-01: C.P. Viet Nam and Westbridge joined. Per the search summary, this brought the total to 26 MOUs and about 4.5B shrimp a year. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/cpvietnam-westbridge-food-group-join-shrimp-welfare-project-electrical-stunning-programme)
- One article says SWP's free-stunner offer ran until the end of 2025. Terms may have changed since, which could slow new sign-ups. I could not confirm this. [SWP HSI page](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/si-hsi-web)

### 4. Base rates and trend
- Headline history:
  - 2025 (ACE 2025 review): ~3.3B
  - 2025-09-16: ~4.0B, 21st MOU
  - 2025-12: ~4.5B, 26 MOUs
  - 2026-08: ~6.1B
  - 2026-09: 6.3B
  - About 2026-10/11: 6.5B, 37 agreements
- Sources: [ACE](https://animalcharityevaluators.org/charity-review/shrimp-welfare-project/), [SWP Sept 2025](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/major-milestone-for-humane-slaughter-shrimp-welfare-project-expected-to-help-4-billion-shrimps-annually-new-mou-with-camimex-seafood-connection)
- Growth from Sept 2025 to Nov 2026 was about +2.5B in 14 months, or ~0.18B a month. The pace was uneven:
  - Dec 2025 to Aug 2026: ~+1.6B in 8 months
  - Aug to Nov 2026: ~+0.4B in 3 months
- Straight-line arithmetic, not a forecast: 7.7 more months at 0.13 to 0.2B a month would add about 1.0 to 1.5B.
- On average each agreement adds about 0.15 to 0.2B. One large producer can add over 1B; Honduras alone is 1.3B.
- Seasonality: none in the metric itself. It depends on when agreements are signed and when the page is updated. No multi-year seasonal record exists.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on SWP's Shrimpact. None of the Kalshi markets supplied with the question are relevant; they cover farm bill, Prop 40, trade deals and similar topics.
- The Metaculus question range (6.95B to 12.05B) suggests the question author expected growth. I found no Metaculus community forecast value.
- I found no specific 2027 target from SWP or ACE.
  - ACE says SWP could usefully spend up to about $3.6M a year in 2026 and 2027, including on a cheaper stunner and on reserves to deploy many stunners if the chance arises. [ACE](https://animalcharityevaluators.org/charity-review/shrimp-welfare-project/)
  - SWP's EA Forum posts set out a long-run "path to 100 billion shrimps per year", a 2030 vision. [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/PHgbyFu4ikJRKPqx9/shrimp-welfare-project-s-path-to-helping-100-billion-shrimps), [2030 vision](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/Ztqzt4BWMPZW5ECfP/shrimp-welfare-project-s-2030-vision-and-absorbency-plans) (the 2030 post returned a 429 error, so I couldn't read it)

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- New agreements in Vietnam, India, Latin America and Africa would raise the headline. Seafood Expo North America (March 2027) and Seafood Expo Global in Barcelona (April/May 2027) are typical times for announcements.
- ACE's 2026 recommendations, expected late November or December 2026, may give updated figures.
- SWP fundraising rounds (Giving Tuesday, year-end) often come with milestone announcements, like the "4 years, 4 billion" campaign.
- Risks:
  - A methodology revision, such as changing the shrimp-per-tonne conversion or excluding non-operational stunners.
  - Agreements being cancelled.
  - A change in how the page shows the headline. If only a range is shown, the question resolves at the midpoint; the current range midpoint is 6.75B.
- Weather is not relevant.

- **Trend:** about +2.5 billion over 14 months (September 2025 to November 2026), roughly 0.18 billion a month. That is about +1.4 billion over a 7.7-month stretch like the time to resolution. Growth has come in steps, around 0.5 billion a quarter, with a faster jump between December 2025 and August 2026 (+1.6 billion).

- **Seasonality:** none meaningful. Changes depend on when deals are signed. There aren't 3 to 5 years of comparable history; the page only dates back to about 2024.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 7.7 months until the July 1, 2027 check. Forecasts close June 1, 2027.

(b) **Latest known value:** About 6.5 billion shrimp per year, from the Shrimpact page, likely updated in October 2026 (fetched 2026-11-11). It covers 37 agreements, and the stated range is 4.5 to 9 billion.

(c) **If nothing changed:** 6.5 billion (6,500,000,000).

(d) **If the current trend continued:**
- The 14-month average is about 0.18 billion per month.
- The recent pace from August to November 2026 is about 0.13 billion per month.
- Extending these for 7.7 months adds roughly 1.0 to 1.4 billion, which gives about 7.5 to 7.9 billion.
- The pace may be slowing: the free-stunner offer may have ended in 2025, and the most recent increments are smaller. That argues for something near the lower end, around 7.4 to 7.6 billion.

(e) **Historical variation:**
- Over comparable windows the figure has risen by 0.4 to 1.6 billion.
- It moves in steps as agreements are signed or the page is updated.
- Single large producers have added over 1 billion; Honduras alone accounts for about 1.3 billion.
- No downward revisions have been observed.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:**
- There are no markets on this quantity.
- The question's range of 6.95 to 12.05 billion implies the author expected growth.
- SWP's long-run 100-billion vision and ACE's room-for-funding estimates suggest an organization that is still expanding.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** SWP revises its methodology, for example by counting only commissioned stunners (about 3.6 billion) or changing the shrimp-per-tonne conversion. Agreements could also lapse, or the page could go unupdated and stay at 6.5 billion. A drop to around 6 billion or below is plausible but unlikely.
- **High:** One or two very large integrators sign, for example a big Ecuadorian, Indian or Chinese producer, or a large Vietnamese conglomerate. Retailer-driven sourcing could also be counted. Either could push the figure to 10 to 12 billion or more.
